A wave packet is formed by the superposition of waves with slightly different angular frequencies $\omega$ and propagation constants $k$. 

Let the phase velocity be $v_p = \frac{\omega}{k}$, so $\omega = k v_p$.
The group velocity $v_g$ is defined as the velocity of the envelope of the wave packet:
$$v_g = \frac{d\omega}{dk}$|

Since $\omega = 2\pi \nu$ and $k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}$, we can also express group velocity in terms of wavelength $\lambda$:
$$v_g = v_p - \lambda \frac{dv_p}{d\lambda}$$
proTip: Clearly distinguish between phase velocity ($v_p = \omega/k$) and group velocity ($v_g = d\omega/dk$).
